# sq-84 — Trim the cut-contract summaries to pointers

The user guide's "Reading only a prefix" states the cut contract in full. `docs/design.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` section 2 and the scope section of `docs/descriptor.md` repeat fairly full summaries of it, and each copy is another place to drift (sq-73 needed six fix rounds, several of them docs wording). Trim design.md and how-it-works to a short statement plus a pointer; descriptor.md keeps the normative part (what `scope.bytesRead`, the cut and the charset rule mean for the descriptor) and points to the user guide for the rest. **Not in this slice:** changing the contract, the user guide text, or any code; touching the breaking-changes entry of the user guide.

## Why

From the sq-73 gate (later #3) and architect A10. Fewer copies of the same contract means fewer doc claims that can contradict one another.

## Files

- `docs/design.md` (the prefix / byte-limit text), `docs/how-it-works.md` section 2 (and any diagram label that restates the rule), `docs/descriptor.md` (the `scope` section; the sentences on the cut rule, the first-record refusal and the sniff-of-the-window caveat). The user guide anchor `docs/user-guide.md#reading-only-a-prefix` is the target of the pointers and is not edited.
- The docs tests in `tests/squalify.Cli.Tests/DocsTests.cs` if one pins a sentence or an anchor that the trim removes.

## Failing tests

No new product test. Before editing, run the docs tests (`Docs_*` and any link or anchor check) in the worktree and note the baseline. If a pointer target is not pinned, add one docs test that fails when `user-guide.md` has no `Reading only a prefix` heading that the pointers use (watch it fail by pointing at a wrong anchor, then fix). A test that pinned a removed sentence is updated to pin the pointer instead, and the change is reported as a deviation.

## Implement

1. List every restatement of the cut contract in the three files with its line, and classify it: normative (descriptor.md keeps it) or summary (shrinks to a pointer).
2. Trim, keeping the facts a reader of that page needs (what the descriptor records), not the full decision tree. Use one consistent pointer sentence.
3. Check `docs/how-it-works.md` and its Mermaid diagrams for drift against the code and the user guide after the trim; report drift as a finding (AGENTS.md Docs rule).
4. No sentence may be left that contradicts the user guide: the breaking-change list there stays the source of truth for what changed in 1.1.0.
